newsitem.title: USA: US CORP BONDS - Trading subdued, players reevaluate.
newsitem.headline: US CORP BONDS - Trading subdued, players reevaluate.

text.p: Trading in the corporate bond high-grade secondary arena remained subdued on Monday despite recovering stock and bond markets, traders said.

"Everyone was expecting a flight to quality (from stocks to bonds) after Friday's selloff in the stock market," said one high-grade trader. "But, that didn't materialize ... so players are now reevaluating where they're going to go."
Stock prices, which plunged 247 points on Friday, erased midday losses to gain 108.70 points by the close of trade.
U.S. Treasuries also ended higher, with the benchmark 30-year bond rising 11/32 at 98-3/32 to yield 6.52 percent.
Corporate spreads to U.S. Treasuries remained unchanged across most maturities, players said.

Trading activity is expected to remain light ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) policy-setting meeting, players said. Most market participants expect no change in the level of short-term interest rates.

In the primary sector for high-grade issues, no new names circulated the market on Monday. Players said, however, if the yield on the long bond dips below the critical 6.50 percent level issuers may return.
"Right now most business is slated to come from the junk sector," said one dealer. "If rates come back down a bit we may see some investment grade offerings but for now that sector's very quiet."
About $2.2 billion in new junk supply is expected to come to market later in the week, syndicate players said.
Among this week's batch of new junk deals is Southern Foods Group's $150 million 10-year 144a senior subordinated note deal via Chase Securities.
Price talk on the issue is seen between 325-350 basis points, syndicate sources said.
Anaconda Nickel will issue a $400 million two-part 144a debt offering for its Murrin Murrin mining project via Natwest Capital Markets, sources said.
The deal is expected to include $300 million in 10-year senior secured fixed-rate notes and $100 million in nine-year senior secured floating-rate notes, sources said.
Another large debt offering will come from Cablevision Systems Corp. The deal is expected to include $300 million 12-year 144a senior debentures via Bear Stearns and Merrill Lynch, sources said.
Golden Ocean Group will sell $150 million in a four-year 144a senior subordinated note offering, sources said.

Among other junk deals expected to come to market this week are: Bay View Capital's $100 million 10-year note deal via Merrill Lynch, Delta Mills' $150 million 10-year 144a notes via NationsBanc Capital Markets, Giant Industries' $125 million 10-year 144a notes via UBS Securities and Dyersburg Corp's $125 million 10-year 144a notes via Bear Stearns, syndicate sources said.
In the broader secondary junk arena, prices were flat to slightly softer in very thin volume as players mostly focused on the new issue calendar, traders said.
(( -- Nancy Leinfuss, U.S. corporate bond unit,
